title: Ops Sentinel: runbook-as-actions + admin utility suite
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Build 'Ops Sentinel' — a lightweight admin utility suite that compiles vetted runbooks into discrete, auditable actions (runbook-as-actions) and exposes them via: (a) a developer-friendly CLI for engineers to execute safe remediations, (b) a Playbook Runner microservice for automated triggers, and (c) a console integration for one-click ops from incident pages. The goal is to reduce mean time to remediation (MTTR) for common incidents while maintaining provenance, RBAC, and dry-run safety.

Scope and deliverables:
- Schema: Define a compact runbook-as-data schema (YAML/JSON) with typed inputs, preconditions, post-checks, and rollback steps.
- Runner: Implement Playbook Runner (serverless-first) with a typed execution graph, step-level idempotency, and an action sandbox.
- CLI: Admin CLI that validates runbook inputs, runs dry-runs, executes with a confirmation flow, and uploads provenance to the ledger.
- Console integration: Add a contextual 'Run Sentinel Action' button in the Ops Console incident view with permission gating.
- Migration: Convert ~25 high-signal runbooks from the SRE handbook into runbook actions (prioritize DB failover, cache flush, worker restart, quota bump).
- Telemetry & audits: Emit structured telemetry for every step (step_id, duration_ms, status, actor, request_id) and centralize audit logs to our existing logging pipeline.
- Simulation harness: Shipping a simulated 'dry-run' environment for oncall training and regression testing on CI.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Stateful vs stateless runner: We chose a stateless runner pattern with ephemeral execution context stored in Redis + durable provenance in the ledger. Trade-off: simpler horizontal scaling vs added small-window state reconstruction on retries.
- Secrets handling: Steps requiring secrets must reference KMS-backed parameter names; the runner fetches secrets at execution time and never persists plaintext.
- Triggering backend: Initially implement a webhook/queue model using Kafka topics (existing infra) to accept alerts -> runner. Considered SQS; rejected because of our multi-region fanout and strict ordering needs for some sequences.
- Language/runtime: Runner in Go for low-latency cold start and easier binary deployment in Dedicated environments; CLI in TypeScript Node to align with existing dev workflows.

Progress updates (chronological):
2025-01-09: Kickoff sync with SRE and Console PM. Collected 34 candidate runbooks; prioritized 25.
2025-01-15: First draft of runbook schema (proto) completed. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Ops+Sentinel+Schema (internal).
2025-01-21: Proof-of-concept runner PoC executed a 'worker restart' flow against dev cluster; logs captured and telemetry emitted to staging. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/playbook-runner/pull/47
2025-01-29: CLI alpha implemented with local dry-run capability. UX notes from SRE review: require stronger guardrails on input ranges and add a mandatory confirmation token for destructive steps.
2025-02-05: Console button mockups completed; design feedback: show estimated blast radius and previous run artifacts before enabling action. Design spec: https://drive.google.com/ops-sentinel-console-mockups
2025-02-11: Security review kickoff. Threat modeling highlights ephemeral credential fetch, audit retention TTLs, and role separation. Initial mitigation plan drafted.

Open questions / risks:
- Long-running steps: how to reconcile step timeouts with user expectations for 'blocking' CLI invocations? Proposal: CLI supports --async to return immediately with an execution id.
- Rollback correctness: some runbooks lack deterministic rollbacks. Need per-runbook manual review and a 'safe mode' that runs compensating steps in a sandbox before committing.
- Delegated permissions: we must ensure the action is executed under the requestor's identity for auditability; this implies token exchange and short-lived role assumption. Complexity inbound.

Review feedback and action items:
- From SRE (2025-01-30): add canary tier: internal infra-team only -> staged SRE -> oncall. Action: add a 'canary' flag to runbook metadata.
- From Security (2025-02-11): require KMS key rotation compatibility and HSM-backed secrets for on-prem Dedicated customers. Action: create a security checklist and schedule a gating review.
- From Design (2025-02-05): Console UI must show prior execution outputs and link to run artifacts. Action: add an artifacts API endpoint.

Acceptance criteria (for this ticket):
- Runbook schema documented and approved by SRE and Security.
- Playbook Runner MVP can execute 5 canonical runbooks end-to-end in staging and emit telemetry to metrics pipeline.
- Admin CLI supports dry-run, validation, and live execution with confirmation.
- Console shows the run action with permission gating and links to audit details.
- Migration plan for top 25 runbooks with owners assigned.

Next steps (short-term):
1) Finalize schema and add automated schema validation hook in CI (owner: Diego).
2) Implement KMS secret resolver in runner (owner: Claire Nguyen).
3) Wire telemetry events to ops-telemetry topic and build dashboards (owner: Priya Rao).
4) Security review meeting scheduled for 2025-02-18 (owner: Aisha).

Links and artifacts:
- Draft schema & spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Ops+Sentinel+Schema
- PoC runner PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/playbook-runner/pull/47
- CLI repo (alpha): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-cli/tree/sentinel-alpha
- Console mockups: https://drive.google.com/ops-sentinel-console-mockups

Notes for future phases:
- Event-sourced execution history for full step-by-step replay and audit replayability.
- Policy engine integration for automated approvals based on severity and customer impact.
- Cross-account federated run capability for Private deployments with per-tenant approval gates.
